#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
root=$(pwd)
out=build/cost
snapshot=${COST_SNAPSHOT:-$(awk '$1 == "snapshot" { print $2 }' tools/cost.baseline 2> /dev/null)}
[ -n "$snapshot" ] || { echo "cost: tools/cost.baseline names no snapshot"; exit 1; }
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || git fetch -q --depth=1 origin "$snapshot" 2> /dev/null || :
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
    echo "cost: snapshot $snapshot is not in this clone and could not be fetched"; exit 1; }
command -v taskset > /dev/null || { echo "cost: no taskset to hold the run to one core"; exit 1; }

# The cold workloads: a name, the machine's store it runs over, the census tables it takes, then the
# command the census compiler runs in the snapshot. A STORE IS NOT THE COMPILER: every run but one has
# the machine's store off, so its rows are what the compiler does, whatever a store holds;
# `cold-with-store-fill` is the cli's cold check over an empty store, which it fills — the store's own
# price, ratcheted apart, its sites the check's own and so read once, from check-cli. The death
# census stamps a word per 16 bytes of slab, half again the memory a run holds, so the build — the
# largest run, its fns the check's own — takes the site tables alone, under the cap.
workloads() {
    cat << 'EOF'
check-cli off deaths check --counts packages/cli
build-cli off sites build packages/cli
check-program off deaths check --counts packages/std-program
cold-with-store-fill filled none check --counts packages/cli
EOF
}

# THE WARM RE-RUN WORK OF AN EDIT: over the store the cold cli check left, `tapes --findings` of the
# cli is settled; then each edit of one file is made, the findings run warm and the answers it worked
# out again kept (its `worked:` line), and the file put back and the findings warmed back, so each edit
# meets the store the one before it left. The edits and their file are the warm lane's measured
# table's, so a row reads against its design budget.
# kind|text|what it becomes, `\n` between lines; a noop edits nothing.
edited=packages/cli/src/commands/cache.av
edits() {
    cat << 'EOF'
noop||
inline|//! in, its own verbs. The store is a directory of immutable packs, each the|//! in, its own verbs. The store is a folder of immutable packs, each the
literal|    println("avra cache clean: ${compacted_said(dir)}")|    println("avra cache cleaned: ${compacted_said(dir)}")
comment|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }|    // a note\n    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }
body|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }\n    let _ = cache_dir().length

(3) has no observable gap, so I made no commit for it. The speller only shapes "reaches the world" words, and an instance check drops those on both paths. A `check` that calls `println` is accepted silently by both.

(2) turned up two gaps, both now fixed with witnesses that are red before and green after:

- **5bc44a47: a false `annotation.unread_mark`.** The layer refused a mark on the user's own declaration when a dependency's `collect … in closure` reads it. The check only looked in the declaration's own file.
- **afc3e0a8: a soundness gap.** A library const that reaches its program's collect through a fn value was settled once over the library's own closure. The layer accepted a program the old path refuses (`const.trap`) and baked an empty value into the binary. The fix makes the survey walk deferred bodies, and the lazy run's later bodies gather as the run's program.

The flip is the tip again (eb92803e). The warm-edit timing and avrac-a..g plus idioms-avrac are running now.

cd /work/avra; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='tools/witness_program_refusal.sh'; s=open(p).read()
o='''#   differs.why — the paths are known to differ on it, for the reason written there: it is said
#     and not failed while it differs, and FAILS once it holds, until the file is taken away.'''
assert o in s
s=s.replace(o,o+'''
#   layer-only — the old path's words are no law of the language's, for the reason written there:
#     the case is held on the program layer alone, as a form only it builds is, and its expectation
#     is that layer's.''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cat > /tmp/netoff/conv.sh <<'EOF'
# conv.sh <group> <case...>: each case judged before, converted to layer-only (its reason moved,
# its expectation re-pinned from the program layer), judged after
g=$1; shift; cd /work/avra; . /etc/profile.d/avra.sh; export AVRA_MAX_COMPILES=16
sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra "$@" > /tmp/netoff/conv.$g.before 2>&1
for c in "$@"; do
  d=tools/program-refusals/$c
  git mv -q $d/differs.why $d/layer-only
  hadwarn=0; [ -e $d/warns.expected ] && hadwarn=1
  for f in refuses.expected prints.expected warns.expected; do [ -e $d/$f ] && git rm -q $d/$f; done
  PIN=1 sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra $c > /dev/null 2>&1
  if [ $hadwarn = 1 ]; then t=$(mktemp -d); cp -R $d $t/c; (cd $t/c && AVRA_PROGRAM=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR=$t/m /work/avra/build/avra build . 2>&1) | grep '^warning\[' > $d/warns.expected; find $t -delete; fi
  git add -A $d
done
sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra "$@" > /tmp/netoff/conv.$g.after 2>&1
echo "BEFORE: $(tail -1 /tmp/netoff/conv.$g.before)"; echo "AFTER:  $(tail -1 /tmp/netoff/conv.$g.after)"
EOF
echo ok

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'find "$tmp" -delete' EXIT

# what one run of the case `$1` said, its warnings aside, its copy's path said as `<case>`: a blank
# line is said only before what is kept, so a warning goes with the line that parts it from the rest
said() {
    sed "s#$tmp/$1#<case>#g" "$tmp/$1.$2" |
        awk '/^warning\[/ { warned = 1; next }
            warned { if ($0 == "") warned = 0; next }
            $0 == "" { gap = gap + 1; next }
            { while (gap > 0) { print ""; gap = gap - 1 } print }'
}

# whether the case `$1`, which uses a form only the program layer builds, holds on the program layer
# alone: 3 where it does, 1 with what differs said on stderr where it doesn't. With PIN=1 a case
# holding neither expectation is first given the program layer's.
judged_alone() {
    name=$1
    from="$cases_dir/$name"
    (cd "$tmp/$name" && AVRA_PROGRAM=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 "$avra" build . >"$tmp/$name.new" 2>&1)
    new=$?
    said "$name" new >"$tmp/$name.new.said"
    if [ "${PIN:-}" = 1 ] && [ ! -e "$from/refuses.expected" ] && [ ! -e "$from/prints.expected" ]; then
        if [ "$new" = 1 ]; then cp "$tmp/$name.new.said" "$from/refuses.expected"; else "$tmp/$name/src/main" >"$from/prints.expected" 2>/dev/null; fi
    fi
    if [ -e "$from/warns.expected" ]; then
        grep '^warning\[' "$tmp/$name.new" | cmp -s - "$from/warns.expected" || {
            echo "$name: the program layer's warnings differ from warns.expected" >&2
            grep '^warning\[' "$tmp/$name.new" | diff "$from/warns.expected" - >&2
            return 1
        }
    fi
    if [ -e "$from/refuses.expected" ]; then
        [ "$new" = 1 ] || { echo "$name: the program layer's build exited $new, not 1" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.new.said" >&2; return 1; }
        cmp -s "$tmp/$name.new.said" "$from/refuses.expected" || {
            echo "$name: the program layer's words differ from refuses.expected" >&2
            diff "$from/refuses.expected" "$tmp/$name.new.said" >&2
            return 1
        }
        return 3
    fi
    [ "$new" = 0 ] || { echo "$name: the program layer refused it ($new)" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.new.said" >&2; return 1; }
    "$tmp/$name/src/main" >"$tmp/$name.ran" 2>&1 || { echo "$name: its product failed" >&2; cat "$tmp/$name.ran" >&2; return 1; }
    cmp -s "$tmp/$name.ran" "$from/prints.expected" || {
        echo "$name: its product printed otherwise" >&2
        diff "$from/prints.expected" "$tmp/$name.ran" >&2
        return 1
    }
    return 3
}

# whether the case `$1` holds; what differs said on stderr where it doesn't
judged() {
    name=$1
    from="$cases_dir/$name"
    cp -R "$from" "$tmp/$name"
    find "$tmp/$name" -name .avra-cache -prune -exec find {} -delete \;
    mkdir -p "$tmp/$name.machine"
    export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$tmp/$name.machine"
    target=$(cat "$from/target" 2>/dev/null || true)
    forms=$(AVRA_PROGRAM=1 "$avra" tapes "$tmp/$name" --new-only 2>/dev/null)
    [ -z "$forms" ] || { judged_alone "$name"; return $?; }
    if [ -n "$target" ]; then
        (cd "$tmp/$name" && AVRA_PROGRAM=0 "$avra" build --target "$target" . >"$tmp/$name.old" 2>&1)
    else
        (cd "$tmp/$name" && AVRA_PROGRAM=0 "$avra" check . >"$tmp/$name.old" 2>&1)
    fi
    old=$?
    (cd "$tmp/$name" && AVRA_PROGRAM=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 "$avra" build ${target:+--target "$target"} . >"$tmp/$name.new" 2>&1)
    new=$?
    said "$name" old >"$tmp/$name.old.said"
    said "$name" new >"$tmp/$name.new.said"
    if [ -n "$target" ] && [ "$old" = 2 ] && [ "$new" = 2 ] && cmp -s "$tmp/$name.old.said" "$tmp/$name.new.said"; then
        return 2
    fi
    if [ "${PIN:-}" = 1 ] && [ ! -e "$from/refuses.expected" ] && [ ! -e "$from/prints.expected" ]; then
    done
else
    names=$(cases)
    leftovers_in "$cases_dir" | sed 's/^/witness_program_refusal: leftover /'
fi
known=0
untooled=0
alone=0
for name in $names; do
    why="$cases_dir/$name/differs.why"
    judged "$name" 2>"$tmp/$name.why"
    judgement=$?
    if [ "$judgement" = 3 ]; then
        held=$((held + 1))
        alone=$((alone + 1))
    elif [ "$judgement" = 2 ]; then
        echo "$name: untooled — no toolchain here for $(cat "$cases_dir/$name/target"); both paths refuse alike"
        untooled=$((untooled + 1))
    elif [ "$judgement" = 0 ]; then
        if [ -e "$why" ]; then
            echo "$name: holds now, yet differs.why says the paths differ — take the file away"
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        else
            held=$((held + 1))
        fi
    elif [ -e "$why" ]; then
        echo "$name: known to differ — $(head -1 "$why")"
        known=$((known + 1))
    else
        cat "$tmp/$name.why"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
    fi
done
echo "witness_program_refusal: $held of $((held + failed + known)) cases hold, $known known to differ, $failed failing$([ "$untooled" = 0 ] || echo ", $untooled untooled"); $alone skipped by the old path (a form only the program layer builds), held on the program layer alone"
[ "$failed" = 0 ]

fn walked_from(
    survey: TaskSurvey,
    root: LoweredFn,
    checks: TaskChecks,
    missed: Cell<List<Missed>>?,
    going_past: bool,
    program: string?,
    lazy: bool = false,
    home: SourceFileAddress? = null,
) -> Walking {
    walked(
        survey,
        every_callee_of(root)
            .concat(hosted_in(survey.engine, home, program))
            .concat(package_hosted(survey.engine, program, home)),
        {},
        held_of(root.wrappers),
        checks,
        missed,
        going_past,
        program,
        lazy,
        home,
    )
}

cd /work/avra; git add -A packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/{item_consts,item_settles,law_findings,item_said}.av packages/std-avrac/src/testing/held.av packages/cli/src/commands/tapes.av tools/program-refusals/gathered_const_traps_as_its_program_gathers_it; git status --short | head; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
program layer: a const each program gathers is settled as its program gathers it

A const whose value reaches a collect gathering `in closure` is each program's own, so it is
never settled once and is built where it's read. A program whose gathering makes that run trap
built clean and trapped only at run time; the old path settles it at compile time and refuses.
Seen with the net off: std-ui's `const web_seats`, for a slider declaring `press`, which no page
delivers (cli ui_view_test's undelivered cases).

The program now judges it. `gathered_broken` runs the const as the program of a named package
gathers it (`value_run` takes the program into `made_reaching`). `gathered_broken_found` finds,
at the const's value, the settlement law its run broke, handed what `settles_broken` hands. The
voice is the const law's own (const_trapped, const_over_budget, const_reaching).
`program_gathered` keeps those findings per file and program. `program_erring` and
`entry_erring` count them, and `file_law_diags` says them for a ProgramFile that names its
program (tapes' `program_file` and the held suite's `named`). The Found→LawFinding constructor
is now the one `finding_of` both paths share.

Witness: tools/program-refusals/gathered_const_traps_as_its_program_gathers_it, the old path's
words exactly. It is red on a049f416 (the layer built it, exit 0). The undelivered program's
check and build now say the old path's const.trap byte for byte, and a slider delivered right
still runs. A warm one-edit build of packages/cli is unmoved (0.57–2.3 s).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJupEEE4E8sXyxX4ypYR
EOF

# Net-off rehearsal: AVRA_PROGRAM_NET defaults to 0 (report only, not landed)

The rehearsal is branch `net-off-rehearsal` = a049f416 + 50421e61. The commit changes two things:

- `tools/gate.sh` `slice_cli`: the forced `export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1` around the cli suite is gone, so the suite runs on the new default. The gate already exported NET=0 for every other row.

Rows that explicitly measure the net were left as they are, because they are claims about the net itself:
- the build slice's net-on cli builds
- the findings slices' NET=1 false-refusal count

Every gate slice was run on gen-2 of 50421e61: 37 slices, which cover the cli suite and the std suites (program, doors-a/b, findings-a..d).

- Tree: 4 cores, `AVRA_MAX_COMPILES=16`, `AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=14000`.

| slice | red | cause | net-related? |
|---|---|---|---|
| fmt | fmt-changed: `net_off_a_doubled…/src/main.av` lex.error | the deliberately malformed fixture. Fixed by e1a3b930 (batch 57), which this branch doesn't carry | no |
| cost | `snapshot 161e52bf… is not in this clone and could not be fetched` | the environment (a shallow clone) | no |
| cli | 9 unpinned cases from 5 test files, below | the net | **yes, all 9** |

Every other slice is PASS: avrac-a..g, program, idioms ×3, sound, doors-a/b, findings-a..d (0 refusals), refusal-a..c, witness-b, warnings-a..c, edit-a..g and build.

### The cli suite's 9: 6 cases where the net hid a real layer gap, 1 a stream difference, 2 a doubled refusal

Each case was rebuilt by hand from its test's own fixture and run with NET=0 against NET=1. **(F)** means a real layer gap that the net was masking.

1. **`sibling_programs_test` :62, :65 (2 cases): F, layer-commands.** A package whose module file `src/stray/stray.av` runs a statement (`println("stray")`) is BUILT and RUN by the layer: exit 0, prints `alpha`. The old path refuses it with `lower.entry_only` ("only the entry … runs statements"). **The layer is missing the entry-only law for a module file reached by `run`/`build` of a lone entry.**
2. **`generated_view_test` :29, :33 (2 cases): F, annotations (mine).** A derive that emits a composition marking its member `@attr` is ACCEPTED by the layer (exit 0). The old path refuses it with `@std/ui:marked-composition` at the template (`formed.av:12:47`). **The second derive (`View`) is never run over a component a first derive emitted.** The old path also says a spurious `type.impl` "`impl ${0}` serves no declared type" in std-ui's view.av, which is its own defect.
3. **`ui_view_test` :167, :173 (undelivered, 2 cases): F, values/consts (mine).** A user slider declaring `press`, drawn on a page, is ACCEPTED by the layer (exit 0). The old path refuses it with `const.trap` on std-ui's `const web_seats` (realize/html/delivery.av:32), whose trap words are the law ("a page names nothing that delivers a `slider`'s `press`…"). **The layer doesn't settle a library const over the user program's rows, or doesn't refuse its trap.**
4. **`build_report_test` :38 (1 case): F, layer-commands, small.** The layer's `build` and `run` print their refusals on **stderr**, while `check`, the old path and the net print on stdout. The test reads stdout, so it sees no headers. Both refusals are said, with the right kinds and places.
   - Same on a package: build/run net=0 → stdout 0 / stderr 1, and net=1 → stdout 1 / stderr 0. `check` → stdout either way.
   - Fix: refusals go to one stream for every command, as `check` does.
   - Side note: under `avra test` this case is red with NET=1 too. There the net's old-path judge runs on the suite's virtual clock and gives up, so the layer answers alone. Worth a look when the net goes, though it goes with the net.
5. **`ui_view_test` :75, :76 (refused parts, 2 cases): R, recommend L.** The layer says all 24 of the library's refusals in the same order, plus one more: `type.variant_lit: Prim has no variant Nope` at `@prim(.Nope)`, beside `@std/ui:not-a-prim` at the same mark. This is the same shape as the doubled case already ruled, `net_off_a_doubled_says_both_true_things…`. If ruled L, the test's owed list gains that line and its count goes to 25. If the lead wants one refusal per mark, it's F (mine): an annotation argument's type refusal stands down when the reading law refuses the same argument.

|---|---|---|

3. **One stale help line:** `std-avrac/src/features/ctxs/semantics.av:32` "build with the program layer (`AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0`)". Its voice is the old path's, so it still holds while `AVRA_PROGRAM=0` exists, but its advice becomes "the default". The wording is ui-language's to choose.
4. **Before it can land, the five items above:**
   - 1 (layer-commands): the entry-only law
   - 2 (mine): the derive chain
   - 3 (mine): the library const over user rows
   - 4 (layer-commands): one refusal stream
   - 5: a ruling, then a re-pin or a fix

#!/bin/sh
# THE avra COMMAND — the compiler, hosted by itself. `build/avra` is
# the working binary; it rebuilds from `make avra`, which uses the
# binary that is already there. The seed is the cold path, and it is
# taken only when there is no binary at all.
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# THE CALLER'S DIRECTORY, kept before this script moves to the tree's
# root: a command that reads "the package I stand in" (`explain`)
# roots there, never at the tree — `cd` below rewrites PWD too.
AVRA_CWD="$(pwd)"
export AVRA_CWD
# the link flags a manifest writes as ${LLVM_PREFIX}
LLVM_PREFIX="${LLVM_PREFIX:-/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm}"
export LLVM_PREFIX
# the static LLVM link's platform answers (packages/std-avrac/avra.toml)
if [ "$(uname -s)" = Darwin ]; then
    AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME="${AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME:-c++}"
    AVRA_SYS_SEARCH="${AVRA_SYS_SEARCH:-/opt/homebrew/lib}"
    export AVRA_SYS_SEARCH
else
    AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME="${AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME:-stdc++}"
fi
export AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME
export AVRA_BOOTSTRAPPING

# A PACKAGE-SCALE RUN — any argument that is a directory — is a
# heavy step: it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs under
# the watchdog (tools/watch.sh), unless it already runs inside one.
# A single-file run is light and runs directly. Judged where the
# caller stands, before the move below.
net=0 1

EOF

#!/bin/sh
# THE WARM-EDIT GATE — the script the DB 07 ticket names
# (avra-8sb5.57.176), and the gap it describes, made refutable.
#
# Its acceptance: an UNCHANGED `check packages/cli` at <= 60 ms and a ONE
# BODY EDIT `check` at <= 300 ms (goal 150), cold process, no daemon, on a
# warm store. Nothing ran it before — `grep -rn warm_edit Makefile
# .github/` answered nothing and no keeper held it — so 374-635 ms
# unchanged and 21 819 ms for one edit stood with nothing to fail.
#
# TWO EXISTING DEFINITIONS, never a second copy:
#   - the MECHANISM is `tools/db_measure/warm_edit.sh`'s: a `check --time`,
#     ONE string literal in ONE body moved to fresh text per round so a
#     round is never a store hit, the wall read from the clock.
#   - the CEILINGS are `tools/speed_ratchet.py`'s budget
#     (`tools/speed.budget`): this script measures and hands its raw stream
#     to `speed_ratchet.py --warm --raw`, the ONE reader of that file, which
#     REFUSES past a ceiling and names each by how much.
#
# stdout is the raw measurement the judge reads (`host <key>`,
# `warm unchanged <ms>`, `warm edit <ms>`); every word of its own goes to
# stderr. THE STORE MEASURED IS THE COMPILER'S OWN (the tree's is set aside and
# put back) and a run that cannot judge is a
# FAILURE, never a silent pass: a named reason and status 1, with the
# `skip warm-edit` marker on stdout. The ONLY skip is a hand-set
# `WARM_EDIT_SKIP` (the workflow's `warm_skip` input), and even then it says
# so loudly. On macOS the measurement goes to the lane's Sprite
# (`tools/work run`), as `speed-ratchet` does — a loaded Mac supplies no
# number, and a worktree with no Sprite refuses rather than passing.
# A cold run clears the tree's `.avra-cache`; the machine store lives there too, or "cold" would read the machine's rows.
export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.avra-cache"
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
# THE LAYER IS WHAT IS MEASURED: its check alone, without the old check the net forks beside it. What
# the net costs is said beside the number, never judged (`net_wall`).
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$root"
avra=${AVRA_SPEED_BIN:-build/avra}
rounds=${SPEED_ROUNDS:-3}
target=${SPEED_TARGET:-packages/cli}
file=${SPEED_EDIT_FILE:-packages/cli/src/commands/shared.av}
lit=${SPEED_EDIT_LIT:-'"build/libavra_runtime.a'}
case "$rounds" in ''|*[!0-9]*) rounds=3 ;; esac

# A SKIP IS A FAILURE. `WARM_EDIT_SKIP` is the ONE hand-set opt-out — the
# workflow's `warm_skip` input passes it, and a human sets it nowhere else.
# With it the reason goes out LOUDLY and the status is 0; without it a run
# that cannot judge REFUSES, with a named reason and the `skip warm-edit`
# marker on stdout.
refuse() { # <reason>
    echo "warm_edit_bench: $1" >&2
    if [ -n "${WARM_EDIT_SKIP:-}" ]; then
        echo "warm_edit_bench: SKIPPED BY REQUEST (WARM_EDIT_SKIP=${WARM_EDIT_SKIP}) — the warm gate is NOT judged" >&2
        echo "skip warm-edit"
        exit 0
    fi
    echo "warm_edit_bench: this is a FAILURE — the warm-edit gate cannot judge; set WARM_EDIT_SKIP=1 by hand only to skip" >&2
    echo "skip warm-edit"
    exit 1
}

# A Mac has no number of its own: this lane's Sprite has. Re-run there, and
# answer its status. A worktree with no Sprite cannot judge, so it refuses.
if [ "$(uname -s)" = "Darwin" ] && [ "${SPEED_LOCAL:-0}" != "1" ]; then
    sprite=$(cat "$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/avra-sprite" 2>/dev/null || :)
    [ -n "$sprite" ] || refuse "no Sprite bound to this worktree"
    exec sh tools/work run "sh tools/warm_edit_bench.sh"
fi

[ -x "$avra" ] || refuse "no compiler at $avra — build it first"
[ -f "$file" ] || { echo "warm_edit_bench: no edit target at $file" >&2; exit 1; }
grep -qF "$lit" "$file" || { echo "warm_edit_bench: \`$lit\` is gone from $file — the edit target moved" >&2; exit 1; }
# The program links the tree's own runtime library; a fresh Sprite may not
# have built it. Built here, on the machine that measures, never a loaded Mac.
if [ ! -f build/libavra_runtime.a ]; then
    echo "warm_edit_bench: build/libavra_runtime.a missing — building objects and libs" >&2
    make -s -o avra objects libs >&2 || { echo "warm_edit_bench: objects and libs did not build" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

# The host the number is keyed by (tools/host_key.sh).
host=$(sh tools/host_key.sh)

# Nanoseconds from GNU date; a BSD date that does not answer falls back to
# Python's clock (the measurement itself runs on the Sprite, where date is GNU).
now() {
    n=$(date +%s%N 2>/dev/null)
    case "$n" in ''|*[!0-9]*) python3 -c 'import time; print(time.time_ns())' ;; *) printf '%s' "$n" ;; esac
}
wall() { # [net] -> "<ms> <status>"; an answer that never came reads as 0 ms and a failed check
    s=$(now)
    AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=${1:-0} "$avra" check "$target" >/dev/null 2>&1
    st=$?
    e=$(now)
    printf '%s %s\n' "$(((e - s) / 1000000))" "$st"
}

# A CEILING IS READ FROM A STORE THE COMPILER UNDER TEST WROTE. A store restored from elsewhere
# (CI's cache, another compiler's run) holds answers this compiler did not make, and an edit over
# it prices their holds, not this compiler's edit path. The tree's own store is set aside, warmed
# here by one unchanged check, and put back when the run ends, so what follows still has it.
held=$(mktemp -d)
orig=$(mktemp)
cp "$file" "$orig"
restore() {
    cp "$orig" "$file"
    rm -f "$orig"
    [ ! -d .avra-cache ] || mv .avra-cache "$held/measured"
    [ ! -d "$held/kept" ] || mv "$held/kept" .avra-cache
    find "$held" -delete
}
trap restore EXIT INT TERM
[ ! -d .avra-cache ] || mv .avra-cache "$held/kept"
# warmed with the net on, so its old check's store is as warm as the layer's for `net_wall`
set -- $(wall 1)
[ "${2:-1}" = 0 ] || { echo "warm_edit_bench: the warming check exited ${2:-1} — not measured" >&2; exit 1; }

# A FRESH EDIT per round, of the same WIDTH every run (a count of bytes written is exact only
# if the edit's text is): the appended word carries a run nonce and the

doors-a    test std-json std-task std-validate std-text std-sql std-queue std-time
doors-b    test std-ui std-http; make ui-host-test and ui-host, std-ui's program tests built and run

findings-b the same on a third of every other package, dealt in turn
findings-c the next third
findings-d the last third

echo "ALL_DONE $H" >> /tmp/gate8.out
sh /tmp/gate8.sh > /tmp/gate8.run.log 2>&1
cd /work/avra; . /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
(AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make try > /tmp/try.log 2>&1)
ls -d tools/program-refusals/*/ | xargs -n1 basename > /tmp/cases.all; split -n l/3 /tmp/cases.all /tmp/cases.sh.
for s in aa ab ac; do AVRA_MAX_COMPILES=16 sh tools/witness_program_refusal.sh build/avra-try $(cat /tmp/cases.sh.$s) > /tmp/wit.$s.log 2>&1 & done; wait
tail -12 /tmp/gate8.out | cut -c1-200; tail -qn 1 /tmp/wit.a?.log; grep -A6 NEW /tmp/idioms.log | cut -c1-200

#!/bin/sh
# WITNESS — `tools/fmt_changed.sh`, THE ONE changed-file fmt check the train
# and `tools/work land`'s preflight both call. Hermetic: a scratch git repo,
# a stub compiler and a stub `git` that records every call, so the proof is
# about the WIRING — which files reach the compiler, which exit status comes
# back, and that nothing ever fetches or watches `main` — never about a real
# build. Run: sh tools/witness_fmt_changed.sh
set -eu
repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
script=$repo/tools/fmt_changed.sh
tmp=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/avra-fmt-changed.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$tmp/bin"
log="$tmp/avra.log"
gitlog="$tmp/git.log"
: > "$log"
: > "$gitlog"
realgit=$(command -v git)

# A stub compiler: records the files it was handed, and refuses any holding
# the marker — the shape a stale binary's refusal takes from the caller's side.
cat > "$tmp/bin/avra" <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$AVRA_LOG"
for f in "$@"; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    if grep -q BROKEN "$f"; then echo "fmt --check: 1 refused"; exit 1; fi
done
echo "fmt --check: $# examined, 0 differing, 0 refused"
SH
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/avra"

# A git that records the subcommand, then runs the real one — so a `fetch`,
# `log`, `ls-remote` or `remote` would be visible, and `diff` passes through.
cat > "$tmp/bin/git" <<SH
#!/bin/sh
echo "\$*" >> "$gitlog"
exec "$realgit" "\$@"
SH
chmod +x "$tmp/bin/git"

(
    cd "$tmp"
    # born on a branch of its own: `main` is then made beside it, whatever
    # this machine names a new repository's first branch
    "$tmp/bin/git" init -q -b seed
    "$tmp/bin/git" config user.email w@x
    "$tmp/bin/git" config user.name w
    printf 'fn a() -> int {\n    1\n}\n' > a.av
    "$tmp/bin/git" add a.av
    "$tmp/bin/git" commit -qm one
    "$tmp/bin/git" branch -f main
    "$tmp/bin/git" checkout -q -b feature
    printf 'BROKEN\n' > b.av
    "$tmp/bin/git" add b.av
    "$tmp/bin/git" commit -qm two
)

run() { ( cd "$tmp" && PATH="$tmp/bin:$PATH" AVRA="$tmp/bin/avra" AVRA_LOG="$log" sh "$script" "$@" ); }

fail=0
say() { echo "witness_fmt_changed: $1"; fail=1; }

# (a) a changed file the compiler refuses fails the check.
: > "$log"
run main feature >/dev/null 2>&1 && say "(a) a refused changed file answered success"
grep -q 'b\.av' "$log" || say "(a) the changed file never reached the compiler"
grep -q 'a\.av' "$log" && say "(a) an UNCHANGED file reached the compiler"

# (b) nothing changed between the same refs — no compiler call, success.
: > "$log"
run main main >/dev/null 2>&1 || say "(b) an unchanged range answered failure"
[ -s "$log" ] && say "(b) the compiler ran with no changed files"

# (c) a canonical changed file passes.
(
    cd "$tmp"
    printf 'fn b() -> int {\n    2\n}\n' > b.av
    "$tmp/bin/git" add b.av
    "$tmp/bin/git" commit -qm three
)
run main feature >/dev/null 2>&1 || say "(c) a canonical change answered failure"

# (d) the check NAMES its refs and never watches `main` — no fetch, no log,
#     no remote query.
grep -Eq '^(fetch|log|ls-remote|remote|pull)' "$gitlog" && say "(d) the check polled a remote, not a named ref"
grep -q '^diff ' "$gitlog" || say "(d) the check never diffed the named refs"

# (e) the `--files` front door — the one a tree with no `.git` (a Sprite)
#     uses — checks exactly the files it is handed, and calls no git at all.
printf 'BROKEN\n' > "$tmp/c.av"
: > "$log"
before=$(wc -l < "$gitlog")
run --files c.av >/dev/null 2>&1 && say "(e) --files refused file answered success"
grep -q 'c\.av' "$log" || say "(e) --files never reached the compiler"
[ "$(wc -l < "$gitlog")" -eq "$before" ] || say "(e) --files called git"

[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] && echo "witness_fmt_changed: 5 proved — one instrument, branch compiler, refs named, main never watched"
exit "$fail"

#!/bin/sh
# THE CHANGED-FILE FMT CHECK — ONE definition, called by the gate's own fmt
# step (.github/workflows/checks.yml) and by `tools/work land`'s local
# preflight, so the two can never drift into two instruments.
#
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head>     # the caller has refs (the gate)
#   sh tools/fmt_changed.sh --files <files…>  # the caller already diffed
#
# Every named `.av` file is run through `fmt --check`. The compiler is
# `${AVRA:-build/avra}` — the tree under test's OWN build. THE BRANCH'S
# COMPILER, NEVER A STALE STANDING ONE: a binary that predates the syntax a
# branch added REFUSES that branch's files and cannot report the canonical
# diff, so it would certify a file the gate then refuses. The gate has its
# own build; a lane's Sprite holds a branch build (`tools/work run`), and its
# synced tree carries no `.git`, which is why `--files` exists. Nothing
# here polls `main`: the refs are named, never watched.
set -eu
[ "$#" -ge 1 ] || { echo "fmt_changed: usage: sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head> | --files <files…>" >&2; exit 2; }
avra=${AVRA:-build/avra}
[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "fmt_changed: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 2; }
if [ "$1" = --files ]; then
    shift
    changed=$*
else
    [ "$#" -eq 2 ] || { echo "fmt_changed: usage: sh tools/fmt_changed.sh <base> <head>" >&2; exit 2; }
    changed=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d "$1" "$2" -- '*.av')
fi
[ -n "$changed" ] || { echo "fmt_changed: no changed .av to check"; exit 0; }
"$avra" fmt --check $changed

# The 35 known-to-differ — triage (read only, on f62f0f88's avra-try)

Every case was run cold on both paths (old `check`, layer `build` NET=0), and each diff was read beside its `differs.why`.
Verdicts: **L** = the layer is right, so it becomes a plain layer case at deletion · **F** = the layer must change · **R** = a ruling is needed · **S** = stale pin: both paths already agree, and only the expectation is old.

**Totals: L 28 · F 2 · R 5 · S 2** (two cases carry two verdicts, so the total is 37. `generator_reaches_world` is L+F and `w_annotation_unplaceable` is R→L.)

## values / annotations — mine (avra-lane-parity-values)
| case | verdict | note |
|---|---|---|
| body_const_budget, const_over_budget, w_const_default_steps | L | the help names the declaring package's avra.toml, where the old path says "the package manifest" (ruling (c)) |
| w_dependency_const_budget_is_its_own | L | ruling (c): a dependency's const is held to its own `[lifted]`; the old path accepts under the root's |
| validator_handed_what_does_not_cross_is_an_error, validator_past_its_budget_is_an_error, validator_that_traps_is_an_error | L | the old path exits 0 silently; the layer refuses as annotation.unsettled |
| builds_annotation_crossing_whole | L | places are item-relative (`main.av#1:55-141`), while the old path hands file offsets. Also the old path says a fns.dead_parameter warning |
| w_annotation_unplaceable | R→L | recommend L: the layer places it at the `@derive` and names the template `@x/c:src/c.av`; the old one places it in the provider's file with a raw disk path and offset (`c.av:545`) |
| generator_reaches_world | **F** (small, mine) + L | the layer's label spells the fn `@std/prelude/src/prelude.av.println`, and it should say `@std.prelude.println` as the old path does. The old path's extra `resolve.unresolved` (`one_stamped`, a twin never made) is a follow-on of the refused annotation, so the layer's silence is L. The differs.why says the reverse of today's output, so I'll rewrite it |

## types
| case | verdict | note |
|---|---|---|
| pw_generic_literal_argument, pw_rest_spread_element | L | ruled: the layer points at the field or element that is wrong |
| spread_generic_seat, spread_missing_cascade | L | ruled |
| sibling_pin_coalesce, sibling_pin_if, sibling_pin_match | L | ruled: a sibling arm pins T, and the layer accepts |
| w_variant_lit_branch | L | ruled: one rule across if/match/when/?? |
| shown_typed_empty_list | L | the old path types a declared `List<int>` as its value `[]` and refuses the answer (lower.no_projection); the layer prints `[]` |
| pw_task_escape_owner | L | ruling R2 |
| pw_lambda_seats_after_parse | L | ruled: a follow-on after a parse error |
| pw_collect_element | **F** (small, types) | same kind, message and place. The layer says the generic `make the value string…`, where the old path says `text is made by interpolation, never by conversion` with the `"${1}"` fix. Fix: the layer's list-element mismatch should reach the old path's int→string voice (the same voice type.mismatch already uses?) |
| pw_const_cycle_unnamed_type | **R** | the same two refusals at one place in the opposite order. Ruling wanted: "at one place, refusals are said in law order: the item's const.cycle before its signature's type.unknown". The layer does this, and I recommend keeping it |
| seat_c5 | **S** | both paths say `this list holds \`int\`, this is \`string\``. refuses.expected still has the old wording. Re-pin it and drop differs.why |
| pw_spread_into_typed_list | **S** | both paths ACCEPT `[null, ..xs]` into `List<int?>` (exit 0), which is right, since int widens to int?. refuses.expected is stale. Re-pin it as a printing case and drop differs.why |

## resolve
| case | verdict | note |
|---|---|---|
| self_lambda_param | L | ruled: the old path's type.method is a follow-on of resolve.reserved |

## layer-commands (the layer parses and lowers each item alone)
| case | verdict | note |
|---|---|---|
| pw_parse_trailing_operator | L | ruled: the item's rule is `stmt`. The layer's help also lists what may start one |
| pw_parse_component_instance | L | ruled for the parse part. The differs.why is incomplete: the layer also says a true `type.duplicate_field` (component `x` declares `x` twice), where the old path says one build.failed head-count error. Update the note |
| select_anyof_arm, select_every_arm, select_fair | L | the old path's `language.defect` (register out of mint order) is an old-path lowering bug after flow.select; the layer refuses before lowering |

## ui-language (the sugar's note frame)
| case | verdict | note |
|---|---|---|
| is_binds_twice, w_match_is_binds_on_int | **R** | the old path adds a frame that explains `if … is` (as a `match` with an `else` arm) |
| pw_chain_apply_argument | **R** | the same, for `f?.(…)` |
| pw_type_hole_text | **R** | the same, for `n.type(s)` |

One ruling covers all four: *"does the layer speak the sugar's own note frame beside a refusal inside it?"*
- If yes: **F** for ui-language, medium (one frame voice per sugar, 3 sugars, said where the refusal falls inside the desugared span).
- If no: **L**, and the old frames go away with the old path.

I lean no. The refusal already names the place and the law, and the frame retells the desugaring.

|---|---|---|

## resolve
| case | verdict | note |
|---|---|---|
| self_lambda_param | L | ruled: the old path's type.method is a follow-on of resolve.reserved |

| case | verdict | note |
|---|---|---|

| case | verdict | note |
|---|---|---|

- If no: **L**, and the old frames go away with the old path.

`wasm_package_c` has a differs.why but runs untooled here, so it isn't counted.

- generator_reaches_world (F): the label spelling of a reached fn. Then the differs.why gets rewritten to the follow-on reason it still differs by.

content.content:
=== body_const_budget
a const's budget is its own package's on the program layer — one settlement shared by every program that reads it — so the refusal's help names the manifest of the package that declares it; the old path's help names no package
=== builds_annotation_crossing_whole
places cross into a compile-time run counted from the start of the item that holds them, the item named after the file (main.av#1:55-141) — an item that only moves hands its generator the same value, so the run is reused; the old path hands file offsets, so a generator printing a raw place prints otherwise
=== const_over_budget
a const's budget is its own package's on the program layer — one settlement shared by every program that reads it — so the refusal's help names the manifest of the package that declares it; the old path's help names no package
=== generator_reaches_world
the program layer refuses (resolve.unresolved: the twin is never made) but doesn't yet speak the generator's own annotation.unsettled the old path adds
=== is_binds_twice
the old path says beside the refusal what an `if … is` with a binding pattern means (a `match` with an `else` arm); the program layer says the refusal alone, in the same words
=== pw_chain_apply_argument
kind and message agree; the old path adds the sugar's own note frame (`f?.(…)` calls the fn when it is held…) the program layer doesn't yet speak
=== pw_collect_element
kind and message agree; the old path places it at the first element of the kept list and adds the text help and its interpolation fix
=== pw_const_cycle_unnamed_type
the same two refusals at one place, said in the other order: the old path says type.unknown first
=== pw_generic_literal_argument
lead ruling: the layer's law is kept — it points at the field or element that is actually wrong, where the old path names the whole argument or list
=== pw_lambda_seats_after_parse
lead ruling: a refusal after a parse error is a follow-on — the layer stops at the parse error, the old path adds type.lambda
=== pw_parse_component_instance
lead ruling: the layer parses each item alone (its design, what keeps edits cheap), so its parse refusal names the item's rule, `stmt`, where the old path parses the whole file; both describe the source truly
=== pw_parse_trailing_operator
lead ruling: the layer parses each item alone (its design, what keeps edits cheap), so its parse refusal names the item's rule, `stmt`, where the old path parses the whole file; both describe the source truly
=== pw_rest_spread_element

=== pw_spread_into_typed_list
lead ruling: the layer's law is kept — it points at the field or element that is actually wrong, where the old path names the whole argument or list
=== pw_task_escape_owner
lead ruling R2: the program layer's words state the law (what owns the task); the old path's are kept as they are
=== pw_type_hole_text
kind and message agree; the old path adds the type literal's own note frame (`n.type(s)` asks the receiver to fold…) the program layer doesn't yet speak
=== seat_c5
a spread `[..xs, "a"]`: the program layer's wording differs
=== select_anyof_arm
the old path also says language.defect (a register minted out of order) after its flow.select refusal: its lowering still runs over the refused select; the program layer refuses before lowering and says the flow.select block alone
=== select_every_arm

=== select_fair

=== self_lambda_param
RULED, the layer stays silent past the naming law: a lambda seat named `self` is refused (resolve.reserved), and the old path then reads the refused name as the receiver and blames the lambda's answer (type.method) — a follow-on of the first refusal
=== shown_typed_empty_list
the old path reads the binding as its value's type, `[]`, and refuses the answer; the binding declares `List<int>`, which the program layer prints as `[]`
=== sibling_pin_coalesce
lead ruling: a generic call's T may be pinned by a sibling arm's type — the layer pins it and accepts; the old path says the call is not pinned by its arguments
=== sibling_pin_if
lead ruling: a generic call's T may be pinned by a sibling arm's type — the layer pins it and accepts; the old path says the call is not pinned by its arguments
=== sibling_pin_match

=== spread_generic_seat

=== spread_missing_cascade

=== validator_handed_what_does_not_cross_is_an_error

# AN INSTANCE'S CHECK READS WHAT ITS RUN CALLS, AND NOTHING IT ONLY HOLDS: a component whose `check`
# calls one fn its instance holds and holds another it never calls, both in a module of their own.
# The fn it never calls edited: the warm build is the cold one, and no instance's check is judged
# again. Taken back, the fn it calls edited: the check is judged again; edited so the check refuses,
# the warm build refuses as the cold one does.
checked_edit() {
    pkg="$tmp/checked"
    mkdir -p "$pkg/src/fns"
    printf '[package]\nname = "checked"\nversion = "0.0.1"\n' >"$pkg/avra.toml"
    fns='export fn fitting(n: int) -> bool { n >= 1 }\nexport fn unsaid(n: int) -> string { "held: ${n}" }\n'
    printf "$fns" >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    printf 'use @std.meta.{Diagnostic, refuse}\nuse fns.{fitting, unsaid}\ncomponent tray {\n    capacity: int = 1\n    fits: fn(int) -> bool = fitting\n    held: fn(int) -> string = unsaid\n    fn check() -> List<Diagnostic> { if (self.fits)(self.capacity) { [] } else { [refuse("a tray this small does not fit")] } }\n}\ntray t { capacity: 3 }\nprintln("${t.capacity}")\n' >"$pkg/src/main.av"
    built() { AVRA_QUERY_TIMES=1 "$avra" build "$pkg" >"$tmp/log" 2>&1; }
    made() { built || { echo "witness_program_edit: the checked build failed:" >&2; tail -5 "$tmp/log" >&2; exit 1; }; unsigned_at "$pkg/src/main" "$1"; }
    judged() { grep -oE 'item_instances_checked [0-9.]+s / [0-9.]+s \([0-9]+\)' "$tmp/log" | grep -oE '[0-9]+\)$' | tr -d ')' | awk '{ n += $1 } END { print n + 0 }'; }
    afresh() { find "$pkg/.avra-cache" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || :; find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete; }
    afresh
    made "$tmp/checked.base"
    printf "$fns" | sed 's/held: /kept: /' >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    AVRA_FOLD_CHECK=1 made "$tmp/checked.warm"
    held=$(judged)
    afresh
    made "$tmp/checked.cold"
    cmp -s "$tmp/checked.warm" "$tmp/checked.cold" || { echo "witness_program_edit: after the held fn's edit the warm product is not the cold one" >&2; exit 1; }
    [ "$held" = 0 ] || { echo "witness_program_edit: a fn the check never calls, edited, judged $held instance checks again" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "witness_program_edit: a fn an instance only holds, edited — warm == cold, no check judged again"
    printf "$fns" >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    made "$tmp/checked.back"
    printf "$fns" | sed 's/n >= 1 }/n >= 0 }/' >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    AVRA_FOLD_CHECK=1 made "$tmp/checked.warm"

# AN INSTANCE'S CHECK READS WHAT ITS RUN CALLS, AND NOTHING IT ONLY HOLDS: a component whose `check`
# calls one fn its instance holds and holds another it never calls, both in a module of their own.
# The fn it never calls edited: the warm build is the cold one, and no instance's check is judged
# again. Taken back, the fn it calls edited: the check is judged again; edited so the check refuses,
# the warm build refuses as the cold one does.
checked_edit() {
    pkg="$tmp/checked"
    mkdir -p "$pkg/src/fns"
    printf '[package]\nname = "checked"\nversion = "0.0.1"\n' >"$pkg/avra.toml"
    fns='export fn fitting(n: int) -> bool { n >= 1 }\nexport fn unsaid(n: int) -> string { "held: ${n}" }\n'
    printf "$fns" >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    printf 'use @std.meta.{Diagnostic, refuse}\nuse fns.{fitting, unsaid}\ncomponent tray {\n    capacity: int = 1\n    fits: fn(int) -> bool = fitting\n    held: fn(int) -> string = unsaid\n    fn check() -> List<Diagnostic> { if (self.fits)(self.capacity) { [] } else { [refuse("a tray this small does not fit")] } }\n}\ntray t { capacity: 3 }\nprintln("${t.capacity}")\n' >"$pkg/src/main.av"
    built() { AVRA_QUERY_TIMES=1 "$avra" build "$pkg" >"$tmp/log" 2>&1; }
    made() { built || { echo "witness_program_edit: the checked build failed:" >&2; tail -5 "$tmp/log" >&2; exit 1; }; unsigned_at "$pkg/src/main" "$1"; }
    judged() { grep -oE 'item_instances_checked [0-9.]+s / [0-9.]+s \([0-9]+\)' "$tmp/log" | grep -oE '[0-9]+\)$' | tr -d ')' | awk '{ n += $1 } END { print n + 0 }'; }
    afresh() { find "$pkg/.avra-cache" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || :; find "$AVRA_CACHE_DIR" -mindepth 1 -delete; }
    afresh
    made "$tmp/checked.base"
    printf "$fns" | sed 's/held: /kept: /' >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    AVRA_FOLD_CHECK=1 made "$tmp/checked.warm"
    held=$(judged)
    afresh
    made "$tmp/checked.cold"
    cmp -s "$tmp/checked.warm" "$tmp/checked.cold" || { echo "witness_program_edit: after the held fn's edit the warm product is not the cold one" >&2; exit 1; }
    [ "$held" = 0 ] || { echo "witness_program_edit: a fn the check never calls, edited, judged $held instance checks again" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "witness_program_edit: a fn an instance only holds, edited — warm == cold, no check judged again"
    printf "$fns" >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    made "$tmp/checked.back"
    printf "$fns" | sed 's/n >= 1 }/n >= 0 }/' >"$pkg/src/fns/fns.av"
    AVRA_FOLD_CHECK=1 made "$tmp/checked.warm"

import csv, sys, os, re, subprocess, shutil, collections
src_tsv = sys.argv[1]; out = sys.argv[2]; avra = sys.argv[3]
csv.field_size_limit(10**9)
rows = []
with open(src_tsv) as f:
    r = csv.reader(f, delimiter='\t', quoting=csv.QUOTE_NONE)
    head = next(r)
    for row in r:
        if len(row) < 7: continue
        if 'annotation.' in row[1] or 'annotation.' in row[2]:
            rows.append(row)
seen = set(); res = []
KIND = re.compile(r'^error\[([^\]]+)\]', re.M)
for i, row in enumerate(rows):
    src = row[6].encode().decode('unicode_escape')
    if src in seen: continue
    seen.add(src)
    d = f'/tmp/rr/{i}'
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
    parts = re.split(r'^// (/w/\S+)\n', src, flags=re.M)
    for j in range(1, len(parts), 2):
        p = d + parts[j][2:]
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
        with open(p, 'w') as fh: fh.write(parts[j+1])
    vm = os.path.join(d, 'vendor/meta')
    if 'vendor/meta' in src and not os.path.exists(os.path.join(vm, 'avra.toml')):
        shutil.copytree('/work/avra/packages/std-meta', vm, dirs_exist_ok=True, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('.avra-cache', 'tests'))
    env = dict(os.environ)
    def run(extra, cmd):
        e = dict(env); e.update(extra); e['AVRA_CACHE_DIR'] = d + '.machine'; e['AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE'] = '1'; e['PWD'] = d
        os.makedirs(d + '.machine', exist_ok=True)
        try:
            p = subprocess.run([avra, cmd, '.'], cwd=d, env=e, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=300)
            return collections.Counter(KIND.findall(p.stdout + p.stderr)), p.returncode
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return collections.Counter(['TIMEOUT']), -1
    old, orc = run({'AVRA_PROGRAM': '0'}, 'check')
    if 'manifest.no_source' in old:
        old, orc = run({'AVRA_PROGRAM': '0'}, 'check')
    new, nrc = run({'AVRA_PROGRAM_NET': '0'}, 'check')
    oo = old - new; no = new - old
    res.append((row[0], i, dict(oo), dict(no), orc, nrc))
with open(out, 'w') as f:
    for r in res: f.write('\t'.join(str(x) for x in r) + '\n')
print(len(rows), 'rows', len(res), 'distinct')

content.content:
Go's `syscall.ByteSliceFromString` answers EINVAL, Python raises
   `ValueError: embedded null byte`, Node throws
   `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE`. Avra traps, with the offset, and never
   truncates and never escapes.

   THE CHECK IS AT THE CROSSING AND NOWHERE ELSE, so both engines
   share it: the native lowering calls this and so does the extern
   frame's text staging. A face that refuses earlier with words a
   program can handle — `@std/io`'s `Holed(path, at)` — is the door;
   this is the belt behind it.

   `Bytes` IS THE ESCAPE: a seat that carries its own length is for a
   caller who means octets, and nothing here touches one. */
__attribute__((noinline, cold, noreturn))
static void trap_nul(size_t at) {
    char msg[96];
    avra_fmt(msg, sizeof msg,
           "a string holding a NUL crossed to C as two strings — byte %lld",
           (long long)at);
    avra_trap(msg);
    abort();
}

#   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
#                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree

#!/bin/sh
# THE PRE-GATE, on worktree /work/gate-wt of /work/avra. Two steps:
#   sh /work/gate.sh merge <base> [ref|file.bundle:branch]...
#       checks out <base> (a ref, or file.bundle:branch), merges the rest in order;
#       a conflict lists its files and stops (the tree is left mid-merge for a decision).
#   sh /work/gate.sh check [--rc FILE]... [--test FILE]...
#       the full gate on the worktree's HEAD, one heavy job at a time, every build cold,
#       every check as non-root user `gate`; GATE_SEED=<compiler> overrides the standing $src/build/avra. --rc runs AVRA_RC_GUARD=1 over a lone program
#       file (evaluator, native old path, native program layer; output vs its .expected);
#       --test runs `avra test FILE`. Each --rc case is also wrapped as a package for its
#       program-layer row, after a positive control that must abort under the guard. Every tools/witness_program_*.sh is run.
# Prints one table (check | result | detail | wall). Logs in /work/gate-logs/<run>/.
set -u
src=/work/avra
wt=/work/gate-wt
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000

resolve() { # a ref, or file.bundle:branch fetched into refs/gate/<file>/<branch>
    case $1 in
        *.bundle:*)
            f=${1%%:*}; b=${1#*:}; [ -f "$f" ] || f=/work/$f
            n=$(basename "$f" .bundle)
            git -C "$src" fetch -q "$f" "+refs/heads/*:refs/gate/$n/*" || return 1
            echo "refs/gate/$n/$b" ;;
        *) echo "$1" ;;
    esac
}

if [ "${1:-}" = merge ]; then

# HANDOFF — lane `avra-lane-parity-values` (annotations and values)

## Who and what
Lane `avra-lane-parity-values` on the Avra compiler, for the lead (controller) reached over the bridge
(`mcp__claude-bridge__post_to_controller` / `send_files`, session token in the bridge note; bundles go out as
`/work/avra-lane-parity-values.bundle`, branch name EXACTLY `avra-lane-parity-values`). Goal: the program layer
(AVRA_PROGRAM default; `AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0` turns off the old-path safety net) speaks every refusal the old path
(`AVRA_PROGRAM=0`) speaks, in the old voices (shared voice fns), so the old path can be deleted. My area:
annotations (validating annotations, generators, marks), values (consts, settlement), enums/match/patterns/lambdas.

Standing rules: commit on the branch, push NOWHERE; no `rm` (use `find … -delete`), no `git stash`/`reset --hard`/
`--no-verify`; `fmt --write` touched .av; a law never assembles prose (named voice fn shared with the old path);
post only at a bundle/blocker/ruling, <=12 lines; gate reds that are not mine are REPORTED, never fixed; every
bundle's receipts = `check packages/std-avrac` exit 0 AND `sh tools/gate.sh avrac-a..g` no unpinned failure, idioms
0 NEW from my files, cli NET=0 build exit 0, witnesses, fmt --check.

## Base and commits ahead
Base: batch53 `d5062c32` (/work/batch53.bundle; prerequisite d750dfa7). Branch HEAD `ac776a62`. Ahead of batch53:
- ac776a62 WIP: the counterfeit-receiver law speaks only where the annotation's arguments name something
- d6889b3c the annotation laws only the net said, said by the layer alone (derived traits' marks claims; trait `Self` as a type variable; trait place item-relative; the 21 `net_off_*` witnesses)
- edeb2641 a validator's computed argument runs at compile time (argument_lifted; broken run = annotation.unsettled)
- ba016bb4 a wrap that doesn't stand is refused (wrap_missing/bodiless/mismatch; externs cross as Fn)
- 2aef1bec callee/receiver laws the net alone said (let-named callee, counterfeit receiver, derive on the wrong kind)
- fac8c8fd an annotation that makes declarations is handed only what the source spells
- ad95e4d7 std/db: a key's run-time refusal names the declaration, never a place
- 1e51f958 a declaration crosses with its places counted from its own item (derived-edit witness green)
- 0e392e26 the annotation rows the old path says and the layer didn't (same-file generator, generated_taken, unfit literal)
Already landed in lead's batches (not ahead): everything up to and incl. c83c540d (Field seats, std-db `@unique(a,b,..)`,
[lifted] budget help, seat-args, validators, record-const crossing, etc.).
Bundle of the above: /work/handoff/lane.bundle (`git bundle create … avra-lane-parity-values ^d5062c32`). Uncommitted
diff: none (/work/handoff/uncommitted.patch is empty).

## In flight and how far it got
THE 21 SILENT ANNOTATION LAWS (switch blocker; list: scratch/annotation-silent-21.txt). All 21 now say the same
`error[kind]` set on both paths (runner: scratch/s21.py, cases rebuilt as /tmp/s21/N) and each has a layer-alone witness
`tools/program-refusals/net_off_*` (21, pinned from the old path, hold 21/21 with the net off).
Receipts on d6889b3c: gate avrac-a,c,d,e,f,g PASS; avrac-b had ONE unpinned failure ("an argument that does not type is
refused as any expression is" — my counterfeit-receiver law added a 2nd error); fixed in ac776a62 (verified by running
`build/avra-try test packages/std-avrac/src/features/annotations`: 185/188, the 3 failing are pinned in
tools/gate/std-avrac.names). layer check 0 errors; cli 0; idioms exit 1 with 0 NEW (27 `ctx.old_path` from batch51's own ctx
tests — REPORTED, not mine). Witnesses on d6889b3c: all hold except `annotation_unresolved` (fixed by ac776a62; passes).
witness_program_edit: every section green; once, edit 5 (cli fmt.av `Walk`) "taken back" failed during the full run but
passes alone (WITNESS_ONLY="5") — a one-off under load, not reproduced.
NOT DONE: receipts on ac776a62 itself (full run), and the bundle to the lead.

## Next 3, in order
1. Run the receipts on ac776a62 (`sh scratch/full.sh`, see Gotchas), then `git bundle create /work/avra-lane-parity-values.bundle batch53..avra-lane-parity-values`, send, and post a <=12-line BUNDLE READY (numbers first). Include: the 21 net_off laws, item-relative crossing (builds_annotation_crossing_whole is pinned known-to-differ: places are item-relative), std-db names the declaration not a place.
2. Promised and NOT done: a type-level `@unique(a)` on a `@model` that names ONE field is a key of one column; its shape line `unique(a)` is unreadable (std-db/src/shape.av `unique_read` only reads keys of >=2 columns). Refuse it in `unique` (db.av) with a voice like model_key_empty: "use the field's own `@unique` mark". Then std-db DECLARED INDEXES over the same `..fields: List<Field>` seat: type-level `@index(a, b)`, recorded as `index(a,b)` lines in the shape text (shape.av shape_text/shape_read), Step.Index/Unindex in migrate.av (diff keys_between, statements, notes), `declared` voices like `model_key_*` in db.av, tests in packages/std-db/src/tests, layer-only witnesses like builds_db_model_key. Tell the services session (via the lead) when it lands.
3. annotation.meta (5 rows, parked for me): /work/package-245.tsv (+ split-*.tsv). scratch/rerun.py re-ran every annotation row of package-245 on batch53: only `annotation.unplaceable` (pinned known-to-differ) differed after my fixes, so re-run it on the new head and confirm annotation.meta is already closed before doing more. Parked singles still parked: `self()` (receiver type absent from method typed nodes), trailing block in a non-fn seat, `Show.lifted`, unknown_prop inside untyped lambda bodies.

## Open rulings / asks waiting on others
- Lead owes: nothing pending from me. I never posted the services-session note for ad95e4d7 (std-db text now names the declaration, `Fact` / `Fact.slug`, never `at …:NN`): the lead asked "tell the services session (via me)" — put it in the next bundle post.
- Asked the warm lane (via lead) nothing yet: the lead asked me to confirm I share ITS placing fn, not a second rebaser. I use `file_placed` / `placed_in_item` / `span_in_file` (item_context.av) only — one placing fn; the item is carried in a crossed place's `Loc.file` as `pkg:path#<item>` (`item_spelled`/`spelled_item`).
- Labelled annotation arguments: the old path types `@f(1, flag: true)` against the next unlabelled seat and refuses it; the layer accepts. Lead agreed it's an old-path defect; left unpinned.
- Known/pinned differences I own: w_annotation_unplaceable; budget cases (body_const_budget, const_over_budget, w_const_default_steps, w_dependency_const_budget_is_its_own — ruling (c): a const's budget is its OWN package's [lifted]); validator_past_its_budget / validator_that_traps (old path silently passes); validator_handed_what_does_not_cross; builds_annotation_crossing_whole.

## Gotchas
- `. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh` first. Env for heavy runs: `AVRA_MAX_COMPILES=16`, `AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=14000` (idioms).
- Build: `AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make try` -> build/avra-try (built by the standing build/avra). If the standing compiler can't build the tree (a bug it carries), bootstrap: `AVRA_PROGRAM=0 make try; cp build/avra-try build/avra; AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 make try`. build/avra-try currently = ac776a62's tree.
- Receipts driver: scratch/full.sh = `sh /tmp/gate8.sh` (copy scratch/gate8.sh to /tmp; resumable, writes /tmp/gate8.out, skips slices already recorded for the sha; ends `ALL_DONE <sha>`) then `make try`, 3 witness shards over `tools/program-refusals/*` (/tmp/cases.sh.aa/ab/ac, logs /tmp/wit.a?.log), prints idioms from /tmp/idioms.log. Run `tools/witness_program_edit.sh build/avra-try` separately. Spec runs and the gate COMPILE THE TREE: no source edits while they run.
- Disk: /tmp/tmp.* witness dirs and caches fill the disk (a full disk makes dozens of witnesses fail with "No space left"): `for d in /tmp/tmp.*; do find "$d" -delete; done`. Container restarts kill background jobs; use the resumable gate script, one heavy run at a time.
- Subprocess probes: set `PWD` to the case dir (the compiler reads $PWD), a private `AVRA_CACHE_DIR`, `AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1`; case package names must differ or the store collides.
- Witness cases: `tools/program-refusals/<case>/{avra.toml,src/main.av,refuses.expected|prints.expected,differs.why,warns.expected}`; `PIN=1` pins from the OLD path (layer-only forms are held on the layer alone); `@std/meta` comes from the toolchain (no dep line); sources must be `fmt`-clean; layer-only forms are `NewOnly` (compiler/item_new_only.av; FieldSeat is mine).
- Idiom rules that bit: closures.pronoun_lambda, compiler.duplicated_message/duplicated_literal, if_expr.when_ladder, fns.dead_parameter, structs.index_compared; private module-level names must be unique across a module; variant payloads take no defaults; `it` fails in nested calls.
- A law is `export law name { kind, reads, voice, warns?, witness, witness_files? }`; voices live in features/annotations/check.av (shared with the old path); worn annotations: `worn_on` / `WornOn` in compiler/item_annotations.av.
- Scratch kept: scratch/ (s21.py, mk21.py, rerun.py, parse.py, tables). /tmp/an*, /tmp/s21, /tmp/svc are throwaway.
- Old branches seat-args, seat-args2 in the repo are merged in; ignore. I'm on whatever model the session runs; attribution lines on commits per the session's reminder.

# Avra — clean-room compiler

## AVRA PRINCIPLES

The spec's Part 0 frames every decision (full text: spec, Part 0).
Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.

- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
- P2  substrate for autonomous services
- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
- P4  Rust-level performance or better
- P5  full-stack vertical integration
- P6  paradox collapse
- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
- P8  escape hatches everywhere
- P9  boundaries are contracts
- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
- P12 one source of truth, many projections
- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
- P17 composability over featurefulness

Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
README.md).

Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape

Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.

## Comments

Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.

## The idiom bar — BEFORE writing any fn

First drafts are written idiomatic, not cleaned up later. Before
the body exists, answer:

1. Is any loop a MAP/FILTER/FLAT-MAP? Comprehension (`?` works in
   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
   push-ceremony.
3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
   loop.
6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.

DOGFOODING.md is the full rulebook; `avra check --baseline
tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`
runs every package, `make idioms-accept` prunes what a fix made

only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted

  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.

  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY

  standard signature and is not a verb.

  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —

  caller's bytes outlive the statement, and is keepable only because
  the caller's own box goes straight through; migrating the WALL seat

  call `.bytes()` — minting a box whose only holder is that call,
  dead at return, handing C a dangling pointer every time with the
  caller having done nothing wrong. The face takes the new type too,

  contract always required. THE SEATS WHERE THIS BITES ARE FEW AND

  second-generation product traps, run the first generation over the
  same source before reading the trap as the tree's.
- THE `avra` SHIM MOVES TO THE TREE'S ROOT, so "." inside a command is
  the TREE and `PWD` follows the move: `docs <name>` and `process`
  (then spelled `explain @name` and `explain process`) rooted at "."
  analysed nothing from the day they landed,
  and read as "no fn declared in this package" for a fn declared
  right there. The caller's directory is `AVRA_CWD`, exported by the
  shim before it moves; a command that reads the package it stands in
  roots at `here()` (cli/commands/shared.av), never at ".", and EVERY
  PATH ARGUMENT is rooted there too, ABSOLUTELY (`rooted`) — a
  relative one read where the tree stands found nothing from another
  directory, and read from a package's own root it walked past the
  `avra.toml` at `.`; one absolute spelling serves both. AND THE
  SHIM'S HEAVINESS TEST SKIPS THE SUBCOMMAND WORD: `build/` is a
